title: Design a Cloud File Storage & Cross-Device Sync System (Dropbox Scale)

spark.summary: Design a Dropbox-scale cloud storage and cross-device sync system supporting multi-gigabyte delta uploads, hierarchical folder metadata, and instant multi-device change notifications.
spark.keyTakeaway: To bound blast radius during partial cluster failures, split the Control/Metadata plane (sharded MySQL + cursor-based delta sync) from the Data/Block plane (CDC chunks in S3), connected by a Long-Poll/WebSocket Notification Service.
spark.byteSummary:
A cloud file sync engine must keep files consistent across laptops, phones, and web browsers while minimizing bandwidth and battery usage.

On the client, a local File Watcher + SQLite index detects filesystem changes, slices modified files via Content-Defined Chunking (CDC), and uploads only missing 4 MB SHA-256 blocks directly to the Block Service (S3).

Once blocks are durable, the client commits an ordered chunk manifest to the Metadata Service (MySQL sharded by `namespace_id`). A Notification Service using Long-Polling or WebSockets wakes sibling devices, which pull incremental metadata deltas via a monotonic `cursor`.

learningJourney.purpose: Separate heavy binary chunk transfers from low-latency transactional folder tree updates.

explanation.foundation: Routing 100 MB file uploads through the same servers that serve folder listings exhausts database connections and API worker memory.
explanation.core: Splitting into a stateless Block Service (backed by S3) and a Metadata Service (backed by sharded MySQL) allows independent scaling of bandwidth vs.

learningJourney.title: Client File Watcher, Debouncing & Local SQLite Index
learningJourney.purpose: Coalesce rapid editor autosaves and ignore temporary lockfiles before triggering network sync.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Client File Watcher, Debouncing & Local SQLite Index** as the intuition layer for Design a Cloud File Storage & Cross-Device Sync System (Dropbox Scale): Coalesce rapid editor autosaves and ignore temporary lockfiles before triggering network sync.
explanation.core: IDEs and Office apps write temporary `.tmp` files and emit dozens of `inotify`/`FSEvents` callbacks per second. The Desktop Sync Client buffers events in a 500ms debounce window, compares mtime + size + hash against its local SQLite state, and only runs CDC when a file stabilizes.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, client file watcher, debouncing & local sqlite index becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Dropbox-scale sync adds LAN peer-to-peer chunk sharing, 7-day grace-period GC, and instant ransomware snapshot rollbacks.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design a Cloud File Storage & Cross-Device Sync System (Dropbox Scale) without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: To bound blast radius during partial cluster failures, split the Control/Metadata plane (sharded MySQL + cursor-based delta sync) from the Data/Block plane (CDC chunks in S3), connected by a Long-Poll/WebSocket Notification Service.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

learningJourney.title: Sharding Metadata by Namespace & Journaled Sync Cursors
learningJourney.purpose: Support shared folders and O(delta) reconnect catch-up using namespace-sharded journal logs.

explanation.foundation: Sharding metadata by `user_id` breaks when two users share a folder—a rename by Alice must appear in Bob's sync stream.
explanation.core: Instead, each root or shared folder is a `namespace_id` (sharded by `namespace_id`).
explanation.deepDive: Every mutation appends to an ordered `namespace_journal` with a monotonic `seq_id`, letting devices catch up via `GET /delta?cursor=seq_id`.

cards.label: Offline Catch-Up
cards.detail: Reconnecting devices fetch only changes since their saved `cursor`.

sectionDiagram.summary: Namespace-sharded journals give every device an exact, resumable `cursor` for delta sync.
sectionDiagram.caption: Every folder mutation increments a namespace seq_id for incremental cursor-based sync.

learningJourney.title: Low-Overhead Change Notifications (Long-Poll / WebSockets)
learningJourney.purpose: Wake idle devices within 1 second of a remote edit without constant battery-draining polling.

explanation.foundation: With 100M connected devices, polling `/delta` every 5 seconds generates 20M QPS of empty responses.
explanation.core: Instead, clients hold a lightweight Long-Poll or WebSocket connection to a Notification Service.
explanation.deepDive: When `namespace_journal` advances, Redis Pub/Sub notifies connected listeners for that `namespace_id`, returning `{has_changes: true}` so clients pull `/delta`.

learningJourney.codeExample:
async def notify_namespace_watchers(redis, namespace_id: str, new_seq: int) -> None:
    await redis.publish(f'ns:{namespace_id}', json.dumps({'seq': new_seq}))

sectionDiagram.title: Long-Poll Wakeup Pipeline

cards.label: Thin Signal

cards.label: Thundering Herd
cards.detail: Jittered reconnect backoff protects edges after regional restarts.

sectionDiagram.summary: Thin wakeup signals via Long-Poll/WebSockets eliminate wasteful idle polling.
sectionDiagram.caption: The Notification Service pushes lightweight wakeup signals so clients only call /delta when needed.

learningJourney.title: Atomic Folder Renames & Cycle-Free Tree Invariants
learningJourney.purpose: Move a folder containing 100,000 files in O(1) without rewriting child rows or creating directory cycles.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Atomic Folder Renames & Cycle-Free Tree Invariants** as the intuition layer for Design a Cloud File Storage & Cross-Device Sync System (Dropbox Scale): Move a folder containing 100,000 files in O(1) without rewriting child rows or creating directory cycles.
explanation.core: Storing full paths (`/Work/2026/Report.pdf`) forces O(N) updates when `/Work` is renamed to `/Archive`. Storing `(file_id, parent_id, name)` in an adjacency list makes folder renames an O(1) single-row UPDATE, while checking ancestor chains in the transaction prevents cyclic moves (`A` moved inside `A/B`).
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, atomic folder renames & cycle-free tree invariants becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Dropbox-scale sync adds LAN peer-to-peer chunk sharing, 7-day grace-period GC, and instant ransomware snapshot rollbacks.

learningJourney.title: LAN Sync, Edge Caching & Bandwidth Throttling
learningJourney.purpose: Accelerate office team syncs via peer-to-peer LAN chunk discovery and pre-signed CDN downloads.

explanation.foundation: Think of **LAN Sync, Edge Caching & Bandwidth Throttling** as the intuition layer for Design a Cloud File Storage & Cross-Device Sync System (Dropbox Scale): Accelerate office team syncs via peer-to-peer LAN chunk discovery and pre-signed CDN downloads.
explanation.core: When 50 engineers in the same office pull a new 2 GB design asset, downloading 100 GB from S3 wastes WAN bandwidth. Clients broadcast local UDP/mDNS announcements of available `chunk_hash` blocks on the subnet, fetching verified SHA-256 chunks directly over LAN TLS while falling back to CloudFront/S3 pre-signed URLs.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, lan sync, edge caching & bandwidth throttling becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Dropbox-scale sync adds LAN peer-to-peer chunk sharing, 7-day grace-period GC, and instant ransomware snapshot rollbacks.

learningJourney.title: Point-in-Time Ransomware Rollback & Cold Tiering
learningJourney.purpose: Restore an entire folder tree to a prior timestamp using immutable revision journals.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Point-in-Time Ransomware Rollback & Cold Tiering** as the intuition layer for Design a Cloud File Storage & Cross-Device Sync System (Dropbox Scale): Restore an entire folder tree to a prior timestamp using immutable revision journals.
explanation.core: If ransomware encrypts 10,000 synced files, clients upload encrypted chunks as new revisions (`rev + 1`) while the old CDC chunks remain untouched in S3 during the 30-day retention window. Rolling back simply replays the `namespace_journal` in reverse to point `head_rev` back to pre-attack manifests in seconds.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, point-in-time ransomware rollback & cold tiering becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Dropbox-scale sync adds LAN peer-to-peer chunk sharing, 7-day grace-period GC, and instant ransomware snapshot rollbacks.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should cloud file sync metadata be sharded by `namespace_id` (root/shared folder) instead of `user_id`?

options.text: Users do not have unique IDs in MySQL.
options.feedback: Users have IDs, but shared folders span multiple users.

options.text: Shared folders belong to multiple users; sharding by `namespace_id` keeps all files and journal cursors for a shared folder on one shard.
options.feedback: Correct! Co-locating shared folder trees and their monotonic `seq_id` journal avoids cross-shard transactions.

options.text: S3 requires `namespace_id` as the bucket name.
options.feedback: S3 stores content-addressed chunks by SHA-256, independent of namespace.

options.text: It eliminates the need for CDC chunking.
options.feedback: CDC chunking is still needed for delta transfers.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Sharding by `namespace_id` gives shared folders a single-shard transactional journal and monotonic sync cursor.

knowledgeChecks.question: In the upload commit sequence, why must CDC chunks be persisted in S3 BEFORE committing the metadata manifest in MySQL?

options.text: S3 is faster than MySQL for small rows.
options.feedback: MySQL is used for metadata; S3 is for binary blobs.

options.text: To prevent dangling metadata references where sibling devices wake up and try to download chunks that haven't finished uploading yet.
options.feedback: Correct! Writing blocks first guarantees that any committed manifest is 100% downloadable by other devices.

options.text: MySQL cannot store SHA-256 strings until S3 returns an ETag.
options.feedback: The client already knows the SHA-256 hash before uploading.

options.text: To bypass the client's 500ms debounce timer.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Persisting S3 blocks before committing metadata guarantees referential integrity for all syncing clients.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does a desktop client safely verify a file chunk downloaded from a peer over LAN Sync?

options.text: By trusting the peer's IP address.
options.feedback: IP addresses do not guarantee data integrity against corruption or tampering.

options.text: By computing the SHA-256 hash of the received bytes and matching it against the Metadata Service manifest.
options.feedback: Correct! Content-addressable SHA-256 verification guarantees bit-for-bit integrity regardless of transport.

options.text: By checking only the file's byte length.
options.feedback: Length alone cannot detect bit flips or tampering.

options.text: By re-uploading the chunk to S3.
options.feedback: Re-uploading defeats the purpose of LAN Sync.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Verifying the SHA-256 digest against the authoritative manifest makes LAN peer fetching tamper-proof.

beginner.summary: A cloud sync system splits file storage (S3) from folder info (database) and notifies your other devices when a file changes.
beginner.keyTakeaway: To bound blast radius during partial cluster failures, split the Control/Metadata plane (sharded MySQL + cursor-based delta sync) from the Data/Block plane (CDC chunks in S3), connected by a Long-Poll/WebSocket Notification Service.
beginner.byteSummary: When you save a file, the app on your laptop uploads only the changed pieces to cloud storage, updates the file list in a database, and sends a quick ping to your phone so it knows to download the update.

intermediate.summary: Split Block Service (CDC + S3) and Metadata Service (namespace-sharded MySQL journals) with Long-Poll/WebSocket wakeups.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: To bound blast radius during partial cluster failures, split the Control/Metadata plane (sharded MySQL + cursor-based delta sync) from the Data/Block plane (CDC chunks in S3), connected by a Long-Poll/WebSocket Notification Service.
intermediate.byteSummary: Clients debounce local file events, upload missing CDC blocks to S3, and commit manifests to namespace-sharded MySQL. Thin Redis Pub/Sub wakeups trigger `/delta?cursor=` pulls, while adjacency-list parent pointers make folder moves O(1).

advanced.summary: Dropbox-scale sync adds LAN peer-to-peer chunk sharing, 7-day grace-period GC, and instant ransomware snapshot rollbacks.
advanced.keyTakeaway: To bound blast radius during partial cluster failures, split the Control/Metadata plane (sharded MySQL + cursor-based delta sync) from the Data/Block plane (CDC chunks in S3), connected by a Long-Poll/WebSocket Notification Service.
advanced.byteSummary: By combining content-addressable S3 blocks with immutable revision journals, the platform supports instant point-in-time ransomware recovery and SHA-256-verified LAN sync while preventing TOCTOU deletion races via grace-period GC.
